overview: After disasters, the Small Business Administration (SBA) offers low-interest disaster loans to businesses, nonprofits, homeowners, and renters to help them recover. The SBA runs this work through regional disaster field operations centers, which put out press releases and fact sheets. This bill would require the SBA, within 180 days, to set procedures so those materials consistently give accurate and current information about loan terms and any changes in eligibility rules. The procedures would include standard templates, a check before release that materials are up to date, and a yearly review for consistency across centers, and the SBA would notify Congress when it sets or significantly changes the procedures. As of October 9, 2026, a House committee had approved it and it was placed on the House calendar for a vote.
for: Supporters say disaster survivors need clear, correct information quickly, and that outdated or conflicting fact sheets from different offices can cause confusion or missed help.
against: Critics say this is an internal management matter the agency can handle on its own, and that adding review steps could slow the release of information right after a disaster.
